title: 264. Ugly Number II

examples.explanation: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12] is the sequence of the first 10 ugly numbers.
1 has no prime factors, therefore all of its prime factors are limited to 2, 3, and 5.

hints: The naive approach is to call isUgly for every number until you reach the nth one. Most numbers are not ugly. Try to focus your effort on generating only the ugly ones.
An ugly number must be multiplied by either 2, 3, or 5 from a smaller ugly number.
The key is how to maintain the order of the ugly numbers. Try a similar approach of merging from three sorted lists: L<sub>1</sub>, L<sub>2</sub>, and L<sub>3</sub>.
Assume you have U<sub>k</sub>, the k<sup>th</sup> ugly number. Then U<sub>k+1</sub> must be Min(L<sub>1</sub> * 2, L<sub>2</sub> * 3, L<sub>3</sub> * 5).
